newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nervy traders see sell-off looming in Belgian OLOs.
newsitem.headline: Nervy traders see sell-off looming in Belgian OLOs.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which rose on Tuesday on light but persistent buying despite a good volume of business in the exchange auction, are preparing to face a bout of profit taking after the sustained rally, traders said.
"Many people feel that profit taking is near," one trader said.
"It might continue up again after a light sell-off, but people are getting nervous now," another trader said.
Traders noted that the Belgian market lagged German Bunds only slightly throughout the day despite the high total of 20 billion francs of business done at the OLO exchange auction.
Traders noted that Generale Bank had again been a buyer of 2004 paper in the morning, and that OLO 15 (May 1997) -- which featured at the exchange auction -- had traded actively during the day.
Some expressed surprise that OLO 8 -- also featured in the exchange auction -- had attracted interest despite being relatively expensive.
At the OLO auction, participants exchanged the May 1997 (OLO 15) and August 1997 (OLO 8) linear bonds against the June 2001 (OLO 7) and March 2007 (OLO 26) bonds.
The exchange of OLO 15 against OLO 7 totalled 9.32 billion francs and against OLO 26 it was 6.72 billion. The exchange of OLO 8 against OLO 26 totalled 4.76 billion francs.
The benchmark 2006 OLO ended the day yielding 6.06 percent against 6.11 on Monday, with the spread over Bunds at seven basis points against eight.
The front month futures contract was 24 basis points higher at 119.61.
